title: Order Parameter φ for the TAD Hierarchy: Chromatin Graph Percolation and Linear Discriminant Analysis
content: Geometric methods (Poincaré embedding, directionality index, insulation score) describe what changes in the TAD hierarchy upon cell transformation, but do not provide a scalar parameter characterizing the mechanism of reorganization. We propose an order parameter φ based on a physical model of chromatin graph percolation. We show that a percolation transition exists at min_sep = 1 (tc ≈ 1%, S(∞) ≈ 0.945) but does not discriminate between cell lines due to the diagonal backbone of Hi-C. As the main parameter, we propose φLDA  - the projection onto the frst discriminant axis of LDA trained on features (contact count, degree in the top-20% graph, PC1, Poincar´e radius). On three chromosomes (chr17, chr19, chr1), φLDA shifts signifcantly under MCF10A → MCF7 transformation: ∆φ = +0.49/ +0.97/ + 0.54 (p = 10−4, Cohen’s d = 0.32–0.89). The shift is linearly uncorrelated with geometry: |corr(φLDA, rnorm)| < 0.2. The link to A/B compartments is weak (|corr| < 0.3) with a sign fip between lines, indicating compartment reorientation upon transformation. The parameter is robust to feature composition (CV < 7%) and consistent with logistic regression (Pearson r = 0.993–1.000 across the three chromosomes); Random Forest achieves higher classifcation accuracy (AUC 0.95–0.98) but does not provide an interpretable axis. At 100 kb resolution (8 GSE63525 lines), the direction of the shift is preserved, but the absolute values of φLDA depend on resolution. φLDA complements the geometric metrics of our previous work [1] as an independent physical order parameter.
